NASB.1: 'Do you know the time the mountain goats give birth? Do you observe the calving of the deer?
NASB.2: 'Can you count the months they fulfill, Or do you know the time they give birth?
NASB.3: 'They kneel down, they bring forth their young, They get rid of their labor pains.
NASB.4: 'Their offspring become strong, they grow up in the open field; They leave and do not return to them.
NASB.5: 'Who sent out the wild donkey free? And who loosed the bonds of the swift donkey,
NASB.6: To whom I gave the wilderness for a home And the salt land for his dwelling place?
NASB.7: 'He scorns the tumult of the city, The shoutings of the driver he does not hear.
NASB.8: 'He explores the mountains for his pasture And searches after every green thing.
NASB.9: 'Will the wild ox consent to serve you, Or will he spend the night at your manger?
NASB.10: 'Can you bind the wild ox in a furrow with ropes, Or will he harrow the valleys after you?
NASB.11: 'Will you trust him because his strength is great And leave your labor to him?
NASB.12: 'Will you have faith in him that he will return your grain And gather [it from] your threshing floor?
NASB.13: 'The ostriches' wings flap joyously With the pinion and plumage of love,
NASB.14: For she abandons her eggs to the earth And warms them in the dust,
NASB.15: And she forgets that a foot may crush them, Or that a wild beast may trample them.
NASB.16: 'She treats her young cruelly, as if [they] were not hers; Though her labor be in vain, [she] is unconcerned;
NASB.17: Because God has made her forget wisdom, And has not given her a share of understanding.
NASB.18: 'When she lifts herself on high, She laughs at the horse and his rider.
NASB.19: 'Do you give the horse [his] might? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
NASB.20: 'Do you make him leap like the locust? His majestic snorting is terrible.
NASB.21: 'He paws in the valley, and rejoices in [his] strength; He goes out to meet the weapons.
NASB.22: 'He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; And he does not turn back from the sword.
NASB.23: 'The quiver rattles against him, The flashing spear and javelin.
NASB.24: 'With shaking and rage he races over the ground, And he does not stand still at the voice of the trumpet.
NASB.25: 'As often as the trumpet [sounds] he says, 'Aha!' And he scents the battle from afar, And the thunder of the captains and the war cry.
NASB.26: 'Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars, Stretching his wings toward the south?
NASB.27: 'Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up And makes his nest on high?
NASB.28: 'On the cliff he dwells and lodges, Upon the rocky crag, an inaccessible place.
NASB.29: 'From there he spies out food; His eyes see [it] from afar.
NASB.30: 'His young ones also suck up blood; And where the slain are, there is he.'

ESV.1: “Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you observe the calving of the does?
ESV.2: Can you number the months that they fulfill, and do you know the time when they give birth,
ESV.3: when they crouch, bring forth their offspring, and are delivered of their young?
ESV.4: Their young ones become strong; they grow up in the open; they go out and do not return to them.
ESV.5: “Who has let the wild donkey go free? Who has loosed the bonds of the swift donkey,
ESV.6: to whom I have given the arid plain for his home and the salt land for his dwelling place?
ESV.7: He scorns the tumult of the city; he hears not the shouts of the driver.
ESV.8: He ranges the mountains as his pasture, and he searches after every green thing.
ESV.9: “Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Will he spend the night at your manger?
ESV.10: Can you bind him in the furrow with ropes, or will he harrow the valleys after you?
ESV.11: Will you depend on him because his strength is great, and will you leave to him your labor?
ESV.12: Do you have faith in him that he will return your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
ESV.13: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the pinions and plumage of love?
ESV.14: For she leaves her eggs to the earth and lets them be warmed on the ground,
ESV.15: forgetting that a foot may crush them and that the wild beast may trample them.
ESV.16: She deals cruelly with her young, as if they were not hers; though her labor be in vain, yet she has no fear,
ESV.17: because God has made her forget wisdom and given her no share in understanding.
ESV.18: When she rouses herself to flee,  she laughs at the horse and his rider.
ESV.19: “Do you give the horse his might? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
ESV.20: Do you make him leap like the locust? His majestic snorting is terrifying.
ESV.21: He paws  in the valley and exults in his strength; he goes out to meet the weapons.
ESV.22: He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
ESV.23: Upon him rattle the quiver, the flashing spear, and the javelin.
ESV.24: With fierceness and rage he swallows the ground; he cannot stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
ESV.25: When the trumpet sounds, he says ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle from afar, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
ESV.26: “Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars and spreads his wings toward the south?
ESV.27: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up and makes his nest on high?
ESV.28: On the rock he dwells and makes his home, on the rocky crag and stronghold.
ESV.29: From there he spies out the prey; his eyes behold it from far away.
ESV.30: His young ones suck up blood, and where the slain are, there is he.”

NLT.1:
“Do you know when the wild goats give birth?
Have you watched as deer are born in the wild?
NLT.2:
Do you know how many months they carry their young?
Are you aware of the time of their delivery?
NLT.3:
They crouch down to give birth to their young
and deliver their offspring.
NLT.4:
Their young grow up in the open fields,
then leave home and never return.
NLT.5:
“Who gives the wild donkey its freedom?
Who untied its ropes?
NLT.6:
I have placed it in the wilderness;
its home is the wasteland.
NLT.7:
It hates the noise of the city
and has no driver to shout at it.
NLT.8:
The mountains are its pastureland,
where it searches for every blade of grass.
NLT.9:
“Will the wild ox consent to being tamed?
Will it spend the night in your stall?
NLT.10:
Can you hitch a wild ox to a plow?
Will it plow a field for you?
NLT.11:
Given its strength, can you trust it?
Can you leave and trust the ox to do your work?
NLT.12:
Can you rely on it to bring home your grain
and deliver it to your threshing floor?
NLT.13:
“The ostrich flaps her wings grandly,
but they are no match for the feathers of the stork.
NLT.14:
She lays her eggs on top of the earth,
letting them be warmed in the dust.
NLT.15:
She doesn’t worry that a foot might crush them
or a wild animal might destroy them.
NLT.16:
She is harsh toward her young,
as if they were not her own.
She doesn’t care if they die.
NLT.17:
For God has deprived her of wisdom.
He has given her no understanding.
NLT.18:
But whenever she jumps up to run,
she passes the swiftest horse with its rider.
NLT.19:
“Have you given the horse its strength
or clothed its neck with a flowing mane?
NLT.20:
Did you give it the ability to leap like a locust?
Its majestic snorting is terrifying!
NLT.21:
It paws the earth and rejoices in its strength
when it charges out to battle.
NLT.22:
It laughs at fear and is unafraid.
It does not run from the sword.
NLT.23:
The arrows rattle against it,
and the spear and javelin flash.
NLT.24:
It paws the ground fiercely
and rushes forward into battle when the ram’s horn blows.
NLT.25:
It snorts at the sound of the horn.
It senses the battle in the distance.
It quivers at the captain’s commands and the noise of battle.
NLT.26:
“Is it your wisdom that makes the hawk soar
and spread its wings toward the south?
NLT.27:
Is it at your command that the eagle rises
to the heights to make its nest?
NLT.28:
It lives on the cliffs,
making its home on a distant, rocky crag.
NLT.29:
From there it hunts its prey,
keeping watch with piercing eyes.
NLT.30:
Its young gulp down blood.
Where there’s a carcass, there you’ll find it.”

AMP.1:
"Do you know the time when the wild goats of the rock give birth [to their young]?
Do you observe the calving of the deer?
AMP.2:
"Can you count the months that they carry offspring,
Or do you know the time when they give birth?
AMP.3:
"They kneel down, they bring forth their young,
They cast out their labor pains.
AMP.4:
"Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open field;
They leave and do not return to them.
AMP.5:
"Who sent out the wild donkey free [from dependence on man]?
And who has loosed the bonds of the wild donkey [to survive in the wild],
AMP.6:
To whom I gave the wilderness as his home
And the salt land as his dwelling place?
AMP.7:
"He scorns the tumult of the city,
And does not hear the shouting of the taskmaster.
AMP.8:
"He explores the mountains as his pasture
And searches after every green thing.
AMP.9:
"Will the wild ox be willing to serve you,
Or remain beside your manger at night?
AMP.10:
"Can you bind the wild ox with a harness [to the plow] in the furrow?
Or will he plow the valleys for you?
AMP.11:
"Will you trust him because his strength is great
And leave your labor to him?
AMP.12:
"Will you have faith and depend on him to return your grain
And gather it from your threshing floor?
AMP.13:
"The [flightless] wings of the ostrich wave joyously;
With the pinion (shackles, fetters) and plumage of love,
AMP.14:
For she leaves her eggs on the ground
And warms them in the dust,
AMP.15:
Forgetting that a foot may crush them,
Or that the wild beast may trample them.
AMP.16:
"She treats her young cruelly, as if they were not hers;
Though her labor is in vain because she is unconcerned [for the safety of her brood],
AMP.17:
For God has made her forget wisdom,
And has not given her a share of understanding.
AMP.18:
"Yet when she lifts herself on high,
[So swift is she that] she laughs at the horse and his rider.
AMP.19:
"Have you given the horse his might?
Have you clothed his neck with quivering and a shaking mane?
AMP.20:
"Have you [Job] made him leap like a locust?
The majesty of his snorting [nostrils] is terrible.
AMP.21:
"He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength;
He goes out to meet the weapons [of armed men].
AMP.22:
"He laughs at fear and is not dismayed;
And [in battle] he does not turn back from the sword.
AMP.23:
"The quiver rattles against him,
[As do] the flashing spear and the lance [of his rider].
AMP.24:
"With fierceness and rage he races to devour the ground,
And he does not stand still at the sound of the [war] trumpet.
AMP.25:
"As often as the trumpet sounds he says, 'Aha!'
And he smells the battle from far away,
And senses the thunder of the captains and the war cry.
AMP.26:
"Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars,
Stretching his wings toward the south [as winter approaches]?
AMP.27:
"Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up
And makes his nest on high [in an inaccessible place]?
AMP.28:
"On the cliff he dwells and remains [securely],
Upon the point of the rock and the inaccessible stronghold.
AMP.29:
"From there he spies out the prey;
His eyes see it from far away.
AMP.30:
"His young ones suck up blood;
And where the slain are, there is he."

WEB.16: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
WEB.17: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
WEB.18: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
WEB.19: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
WEB.20: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
WEB.21: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
WEB.22: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
WEB.23: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
WEB.24: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
WEB.25: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
WEB.26: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
WEB.27: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
WEB.28: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
WEB.29: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
WEB.30: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”

MSG.1:
"Do you know the month when mountain goats give birth?
Have you ever watched a doe bear her fawn?
MSG.2:
Do you know how many months she is pregnant?
Do you know the season of her delivery,
MSG.3: when she crouches down and drops her offspring?
MSG.4:
Her young ones flourish and are soon on their own;
they leave and don't come back.
MSG.5:
"Who do you think set the wild donkey free,
opened the corral gates and let him go?
MSG.6:
I gave him the whole wilderness to roam in,
the rolling plains and wide-open places.
MSG.7:
He laughs at his city cousins, who are harnessed and harried.
He's oblivious to the cries of teamsters.
MSG.8:
He grazes freely through the hills,
nibbling anything that's green.
MSG.9:
"Will the wild buffalo condescend to serve you,
volunteer to spend the night in your barn?
MSG.10:
Can you imagine hitching your plow to a buffalo
and getting him to till your fields?
MSG.11:
He's hugely strong, yes, but could you trust him,
would you dare turn the job over to him?
MSG.12:
You wouldn't for a minute depend on him, would you,
to do what you said when you said it?
MSG.13:
"The ostrich flaps her wings futilely—
all those beautiful feathers, but useless!
MSG.14:
She lays her eggs on the hard ground,
leaves them there in the dirt, exposed to the weather,
MSG.15:
Not caring that they might get stepped on and cracked
or trampled by some wild animal.
MSG.16:
She's negligent with her young, as if they weren't even hers.
She cares nothing about anything.
MSG.17:
She wasn't created very smart, that's for sure,
wasn't given her share of good sense.
MSG.18:
But when she runs, oh, how she runs,
laughing, leaving horse and rider in the dust.
MSG.19:
"Are you the one who gave the horse his prowess
and adorned him with a shimmering mane?
MSG.20:
Did you create him to prance proudly
and strike terror with his royal snorts?
MSG.21:
He paws the ground fiercely, eager and spirited,
then charges into the fray.
MSG.22:
He laughs at danger, fearless,
doesn't shy away from the sword.
MSG.23:
The banging and clanging
of quiver and lance don't faze him.
MSG.24:
He quivers with excitement, and at the trumpet blast
races off at a gallop.
MSG.25:
At the sound of the trumpet he neighs mightily,
smelling the excitement of battle from a long way off,
catching the rolling thunder of the war cries.
MSG.26:
"Was it through your know how that the hawk learned to fly,
soaring effortlessly on thermal updrafts?
MSG.27:
Did you command the eagle's flight,
and teach her to build her nest in the heights,
MSG.28:
Perfectly at home on the high cliff-face,
invulnerable on pinnacle and crag?
MSG.29:
From her perch she searches for prey,
spies it at a great distance.
MSG.30:
Her young gorge themselves on carrion;
wherever there's a roadkill, you'll see her circling."

NET.1: “Are you acquainted with the way the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch as the wild deer give birth to their young?
NET.2: Do you count the months they must fulfill, and do you know the time they give birth?
NET.3: They crouch, they bear their young, they bring forth the offspring they have carried.
NET.4: Their young grow strong, and grow up in the open; they go off, and do not return to them.
NET.5: Who let the wild donkey go free? Who released the bonds of the donkey,
NET.6: to whom I appointed the steppe for its home, the salt wastes as its dwelling place?
NET.7: It scorns the tumult in the town; it does not hear the shouts of a driver.
NET.8: It ranges the hills as its pasture, and searches after every green plant.
NET.9: Is the wild ox willing to be your servant? Will it spend the night at your feeding trough?
NET.10: Can you bind the wild ox to a furrow with its rope, will it till the valleys, following after you?
NET.11: Will you rely on it because its strength is great? Will you commit your labor to it?
NET.12: Can you count on it to bring in your grain, and gather the grain to your threshing floor?
NET.13: “The wings of the ostrich flap with joy, but are they the pinions and plumage of a stork?
NET.14: For she leaves her eggs on the ground, and lets them be warmed on the soil.
NET.15: She forgets that a foot might crush them, or that a wild animal might trample them.
NET.16: She is harsh with her young, as if they were not hers; she is unconcerned about the uselessness of her labor.
NET.17: For God deprived her of wisdom, and did not impart understanding to her.
NET.18: But as soon as she springs up, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
NET.19: “Do you give the horse its strength? Do you clothe its neck with a mane?
NET.20: Do you make it leap like a locust? Its proud neighing is terrifying!
NET.21: It paws the ground in the valley, exulting mightily, it goes out to meet the weapons.
NET.22: It laughs at fear and is not dismayed; it does not shy away from the sword.
NET.23: On it the quiver rattles; the lance and javelin flash.
NET.24: In excitement and impatience it consumes the ground; it cannot stand still when the trumpet is blown.
NET.25: At the sound of the trumpet, it says, ‘Aha!’ And from a distance it catches the scent of battle, the thunderous shouting of commanders, and the battle cries.
NET.26: “Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars, and spreads its wings toward the south?
NET.27: Is it at your command that the eagle soars, and builds its nest on high?
NET.28: It lives on a rock and spends the night there, on a rocky crag and a fortress.
NET.29: From there it spots its prey, its eyes gaze intently from a distance.
NET.30: And its young ones devour the blood, and where the dead carcasses are, there it is.”

NIV.1:
“Do you know when the mountain goats give birth?
Do you watch when the doe bears her fawn?
NIV.2:
Do you count the months till they bear?
Do you know the time they give birth?
NIV.3:
They crouch down and bring forth their young;
their labor pains are ended.
NIV.4:
Their young thrive and grow strong in the wilds;
they leave and do not return.
NIV.5:
“Who let the wild donkey go free?
Who untied his ropes?
NIV.6:
I gave him the wasteland as his home,
the salt flats as his habitat.
NIV.7:
He laughs at the commotion in the town;
he does not hear a driver’s shout.
NIV.8:
He ranges the hills for his pasture
and searches for any green thing.
NIV.9:
“Will the wild ox consent to serve you?
Will he stay by your manger at night?
NIV.10:
Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness?
Will he till the valleys behind you?
NIV.11:
Will you rely on him for his great strength?
Will you leave your heavy work to him?
NIV.12:
Can you trust him to bring in your grain
and gather it to your threshing floor?
NIV.13:
“The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully,
but they cannot compare with the pinions and feathers of the stork.
NIV.14:
She lays her eggs on the ground
and lets them warm in the sand,
NIV.15:
unmindful that a foot may crush them,
that some wild animal may trample them.
NIV.16:
She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers;
she cares not that her labor was in vain,
NIV.17:
for God did not endow her with wisdom
or give her a share of good sense.
NIV.18:
Yet when she spreads her feathers to run,
she laughs at horse and rider.
NIV.19:
“Do you give the horse his strength
or clothe his neck with a flowing mane?
NIV.20:
Do you make him leap like a locust,
striking terror with his proud snorting?
NIV.21:
He paws fiercely, rejoicing in his strength,
and charges into the fray.
NIV.22:
He laughs at fear, afraid of nothing;
he does not shy away from the sword.
NIV.23:
The quiver rattles against his side,
along with the flashing spear and lance.
NIV.24:
In frenzied excitement he eats up the ground;
he cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
NIV.25:
At the blast of the trumpet he snorts, ‘Aha!’
He catches the scent of battle from afar,
the shout of commanders and the battle cry.
NIV.26:
“Does the hawk take flight by your wisdom
and spread his wings toward the south?
NIV.27:
Does the eagle soar at your command
and build his nest on high?
NIV.28:
He dwells on a cliff and stays there at night;
a rocky crag is his stronghold.
NIV.29:
From there he seeks out his food;
his eyes detect it from afar.
NIV.30:
His young ones feast on blood,
and where the slain are, there is he.”
